text:
elaine: Heads up — after the per-route tag denorm landed we are seeing a large jump in console telemetry writes. write amplification when users edit route metadata is ~2x and it's pushing ingest QPS and our per-tenant quota billing spikes. We need a plan to mitigate before we roll the rest of tenants.

jorge: Do we have a quick breakdown? is this from UI edits or background jobs?

elaine: Mostly UI edits + attribution updates from the sync worker. Each small change triggers a full route doc rewrite across the analytics envelope.

vikram: TL;DR: denorm field is large and included in the telemetry envelope => every change to route metadata churns the envelope (and secondary indexes). We're paying both write and index cost.

tanay: Options: 1) materialize only a compact route_tag id list (no full JSON), 2) move full tags to a separate table with a read adapter/join, 3) introduce a prefix/KV cache and only diff writes. tradeoffs?

elaine: Preference for option 1 + small read adapter for console queries. Keep existing API shape by doing a transparent read-union: prefer materialized column, fall back to tags table. That avoids backcompat changes in the console.

jorge: Implementation sketch: materialized_tags (text[]) on routes, dualwrite route_tags table -> materialized column for N days, backfill job to populate materialized_tags for existing rows. After we confirm read traffic hits the materialized path we can stop heavy writes to analytics envelope.

samir: Important: plan the indexes. If we add a text[] col we should avoid GIN on the full envelope. Instead add a compact route_tag_hash col (bigint) that we index for lookup; keep materialized_tags for display only (no heavy index).

vikram: Agreed. Also: add a write-side guard in the ingestion pipeline so analytics envelope rewrites are skipped if only materialized_tags changed. That reduces write amplification immediately.

elaine: Proposed rollout steps:
1) Feature-flag materialized_tags API read path (console uses flag)
2) Deploy backfill job in shadow mode to populate materialized_tags and route_tag_hash
3) Enable write guard in ingest pipeline to skip envelope rewrites when possible
4) Canary the flag on ~5% of tenants and monitor ingest QPS and console errors
5) Gradual ramp + monitor cost delta then flip globally

jorge: Backfill SQL prototype (run in small batches):
```sql
-- backfill materialized_tags column safely
BEGIN;
UPDATE console.routes r
SET materialized_tags = t.tags
FROM route_tags t
WHERE t.route_id = r.id AND r.materialized_tags IS NULL
AND r.tenant_id = $TENANT_BATCH;
COMMIT;
```

tanay: Also add a checksum column route_tag_hash = farm_fingerprint(array_to_string(materialized_tags, ',')) to detect no-op updates. The ingest guard can compare new hash vs existing and skip heavy path when identical.

infra-bot: migration-bot: scheduled job "route_tags_materialize_backfill" created, runs as batch worker with rate limit 1000 rows/min. Logs -> https://infra/jobs/route_tags_materialize_backfill

samir: Telemetry: define two key SLOs to track during canary: ingest_write_qps per-tenant, and console_query_p95. Also track cost delta and serialize a dashboard in "console/telemetry/migrations".

elaine: UX/Rollouts note: We need the console rollout UX to surface the FF state and show "migration progress" per tenant. Add a lightweight banner in the tenant settings page with progress % and an opt-out contact for customers on dedicated contracts.

vikram: One more thought: for long-term, move analytics envelope to store only stable identifiers and use enrichment service to resolve display metadata at read time. That flips write/read cost. But that's a bigger effort; do the materialized_tags as an intermediate step.

jorge: Risk checklist:
- backfill can be slow -> throttle, schedule low-traffic windows
- read adapter introduces extra reads -> cache at console layer
- accidental index creation -> avoid GIN on envelope
- billing changes -> coordinate finance for tenant communications

tanay: Can we run a short experiment: pick 50 high-churn routes, enable materialized read path and write-guard, measure 24h delta? If it reduces writes by >40% it's a green light for canary.

elaine: I'll open a runbook and assign tasks. Jorge/Tanay/Vikram/Samir can you ack and list owners for backfill, pipeline guard, dashboard, and console flag?

jorge: ack — I'll own the backfill job and index plan.

tanay: ack — I'll implement the ingest guard + hash comparison.

vikram: ack — I'll wire the read adapter and console FF + cache hints.

samir: ack — I'll build the dashboard, telemetry metrics, and cost estimate.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: migration job created and queued (id: mj-20260320-1). Notify #eng-oncall if job errors.

elaine: Thanks team — aim to have the experiment running by next Tue. I'll put owners + timelines in the runbook link: https://go/runbooks/route-tags-materialize

jorge: small note — avoid changing the analytics envelope schema name; do not add new top-level keys until after canary to minimize decoder churn in ingest consumers.

elaine: good call. We'll keep envelope stable and use a separate materialized column.

vikram: copying this plan into the migration checklist. will update when experiment data comes in. :thumbsup:
